consensus_summary: Sea/waters primarily symbolize primordial chaos, disorder, death, and hostile anti-God powers that God subdues (culminating in the sea’s removal); a common complementary sense is the restless nations/peoples/multitudes (via Rev 17:15 and parallels), while ‘living’ or flowing waters separately signify life, Spirit, or cleansing.
book_summary: Peoples and nations as an unrooted mass: restless below the firmament, but gathered above it as the still waters of heaven and the sea of glass.
consensus_core_identification: chaos/disorder/hostile powers (with restless nations as common complementary reading)
book_core_identification: peoples and nations in an unrooted mass
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts the restless-nations sense to waters below the firmament and reclassifies the waters above the firmament plus the sea of glass as the same nations now stilled/gathered; consensus does not equate upper waters or sea of glass with nations and keeps chaos as the dominant default for ‘sea’.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the well-attested ‘peoples/nations’ strand explicitly listed across the consensus alternatives (anchored by Rev 17:15). The book does not deny chaos and therefore does not replace the consensus referent; it simply elevates and conditions the nations reading with a firmament-based partition (restless below vs. still above/sea of glass). That partition and the inclusion of sea-of-glass texts materially alter extension and boundaries without contradicting the shared nations core, yielding REFINED rather than MATCH, DIVERGENT, or NOVEL.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary identification remains chaos/evil (sea abolished in new creation), and equating the heavenly sea of glass or waters above the firmament with gathered nations is an interpretive step not directly supplied by the cited texts.
